title: Pediatric DKA Management

changelog.change: Initial entry from Peds_Module_Content_Spec.md — confirmed K+ thresholds and the < 5 y insulin-rate refinement.

purpose: Weight-based fluid and insulin protocol for pediatric DKA, with the cerebral-edema-driven safeguards that distinguish it from adult protocols.

items: If in shock: 10-20 mL/kg isotonic (NS or LR) bolus over 1-2 hours; reassess after each bolus
Be deliberately cautious with rate and total volume — rapid correction is a cerebral-edema risk in pediatric DKA
After initial resuscitation, replace the estimated deficit evenly over 24-48 hours plus maintenance
Continuous infusion 0.05-0.1 units/kg/h, started AFTER the initial fluid bolus
NO insulin bolus — bolus dosing is specifically avoided in pediatric DKA (cerebral edema risk)
Children < 5 years: use the lower end, 0.05 units/kg/h, to reduce subsequent hypoglycemia
Add dextrose to fluids once glucose falls to ~250-300 mg/dL; do not stop the insulin infusion to treat hypoglycemia — add/increase dextrose instead

rows: DEFER insulin until K+ rises above 3.0 — hypokalemia takes priority over acidosis
Add potassium to maintenance fluids once urine output is confirmed
Do NOT add potassium to fluids until the patient has passed urine or K+ has normalized

body.text: Watch for headache, altered mental status, and a Cushing's-triad pattern (bradycardia + hypertension). If suspected, treat emergently with mannitol or hypertonic saline and do not wait for imaging.

buildNote: Cross-links to the Holliday-Segar maintenance-fluid calculator for the maintenance component. A production build could add a deficit-replacement calculator (% dehydration × weight).
